messages.author: 9ee7ccab51acb1f5
messages.subject: Spatial recaptures
parts:
Dear all,

We are calculating roe deer density by means of spatial capture recapture. We are curretly subsampling our data to test the robustness our density estimates. For each subsampling we plan to record the number of spatial recaptures (= detection of unique individuals at multiple locations in space = cameratraps). 

Could someone give us some information about how we can extrat this information from the output of the function secr.fit, from the capturehistory or other function?  

Thank you very much for your attention.

All the best,

Amael Hinojo

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Spatial recaptures
parts:
Amael
Something like this would work: sum(unlist(moves(captdata))>0).
Note that the number of 'movements' is not reliable if the data include more than two detections per animal per occasion, as the order of the detections is not known. As an example: an animal detected in one sampling interval (occasion) at camera 1, then camera 2, then camera 1 (1,2,1) actually made two movements, but it may appear as one movement (1,1,2). Also, despite the focus by some authors on 'spatial recaptures', I know of no demonstration that this number is more important than total recaptures. Of course the data must include some spatial recaptures.
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Spatial recaptures
parts:
I see now what you were after (not 'spatial recaptures' as I understand it, but that concept is not well defined).

Here are three ways to get the number of animals detected at only one detector:

> sum(summary(captdata, moves = TRUE)$moves$peranimal[-1]) [1] 56 > sum(table(apply(table(trap(captdata), animalID(captdata))>0,2,sum))[-1]) [1] 56 > sum(apply(apply(captdata, c(1,3), sum)>0,1,sum)>1) [1] 56
The last is the most direct - it uses the fact that the capthist object is a 3-D array that you can manipulate with apply() as usual. You can make a function

moved <- function (ch) sum(apply(apply(abs(ch), c(1,3), sum)>0,1,sum)>1)

Then
> moved(ch) [1] 56
('abs' protects against animals that were removed/died)

messages.subject: Re: Spatial recaptures
parts:
A subset of a capthist object (from subsetCH <- subset()) is also a capthist object, so you can use 
sum(unlist(moves(subsetCH))>0) 

to obtain the number of 'spatial recaptures', so called, with the caveats I raised initially.
